## Ctx.renderInlineAnswer() method

Answers the active inline query with caller-built results and template button text.

Template block: `<g-inline-button>` (read via `getGInlineButton`<!-- -->).

**Signature:**

```typescript
renderInlineAnswer(params: IRenderInlineAnswerParams): Promise<true>;
```

Answer params: `results` inline results built by the caller, up to 50 (required); `data` optional template interpolation data (or null to omit); `AGBaseId` template base ID position for the button text (required); `options` optional answer options (or null to omit); `buttonStartParameter` optional deep-link start parameter, enabling the block-text button (or null to omit).


</td></tr>
</tbody></table>

**Returns:**

Promise&lt;true&gt;

True on success.

## Remarks

Result contents are built by the caller from `data` (multilang payloads); the `<g-inline-button>` block supplies the default `button.text` label and `start_parameter`<!-- -->. Precedence: a caller-supplied `options.button` wins first, then the explicit `buttonStartParameter`<!-- -->, then the block's own `start-parameter`<!-- -->. The block is always resolved — even when no button is built — as fail-fast validation that the template exists.

Observe-only send-error coverage (mirrors `renderDice`<!-- -->): failures are classified via `Ctx.classifySendError`<!-- -->, reported to `notifySendError`<!-- -->, and logged (`retryable` → `log.error`<!-- -->, `fallback-text` → `log.warn`<!-- -->). After notify+log the original error is ALWAYS rethrown untouched.

Telegram caps answers at 50 results; cache them with `cache_time` for identical queries.

## Example


```typescript
async handleInlineQuery() {
  await this.renderInlineAnswer({results: [article], data: {name: `Ani`}, AGBaseId: `inline-card`, buttonStartParameter: `start=1`})
}
```
